checks.label: Applying a matrix that only scales each basis vector, say 100 times, scales each one by the 100th power of its eigenvalue: on the eigenvector grid every step multiplies the dot’s amounts by 3 and 2, the D card has 3ⁿ and 2ⁿ down its diagonal, and PDⁿP⁻¹ = Aⁿ for every n from 0 to 10 and for n = 100

A shear does not have enough eigenvectors to span all of space: the shear screen draws one eigenvector line, its grid switch shows greyed out with the reason beside it, and [2 1; 0 2] also has only one line

A matrix with a repeated eigenvalue can be diagonalised provided it has as many independent eigenvectors as columns: 2I has 2 twice and every arrow is an eigenvector, so it is diagonal already, while the shear and [2 1; 0 2] have their eigenvalue twice and only one line

Every worked number is right: A² = [9 5; 0 4], A³ = [27 19; 0 8], A¹⁰ = [59049 58025; 0 1024] and Aⁿ = [3ⁿ 3ⁿ − 2ⁿ; 0 2ⁿ]; 3⁴ = 81; (1, 1) has amounts (2, 1), then (54, 8), which is (46, 8); P = [1 −1; 0 1], P⁻¹ = [1 1; 0 1], PDP⁻¹ = A, and (1, 1) goes to (2, 1), (6, 2), (4, 2); the pumps have 1 along (3, 2) and 0.5 along (1, −1), 200 and 400 lots, tank 1 at 800, 700, 650, 625 and 612.5 L, heading for 600 L and 400 L; det P = −5, P⁻¹ = [0.2 0.2; 0.4 −0.6], A³ = [0.65 0.525; 0.35 0.475]; the shear’s Aⁿ = [1 n; 0 1]; M stretches (1, 1) by 0.9 and (1, −1) by 0.5, and 0.5 × 0.9²⁰ is about 0.06
Each puzzle’s answer comes from the rule, and each wrong answer offered is the slip its hint names
Each puzzle offers three different answers, accepts only the right one, and draws every wrong one in the warning colour
Before Check, no puzzle shows its answer; after a right answer, it does

Each demonstration ends where the lesson says: the flag at n = 3 with A³ = [27 19; 0 8]; at n = 3 on the eigenvector grid with D³ = [27 0; 0 8] and the dot’s amounts (27, 8); (1, 1) to the amounts (2, 1), stretched to (6, 2), back to (4, 2) = A(1, 1); n = 10 with A¹⁰ = [59049 58025; 0 1024]; tank 1 at 625 L and tank 2 at 375 L after 4 hours, 25 L above 600 L; the shear at n = 3 with one line and [1 3; 0 1]

While each demonstration plays, the rule holds at every moment: n only grows; the flag drawn moves straight from Aᵏ to Aᵏ⁺¹ times the flag; the cards read the powers for the nearest whole step; the tanks always hold 1000 L between them

The view zooms out by itself so the whole flag stays in sight: at every n from 0 to 10, for the stretch on both grids and for the shear, every corner of the flag is inside the pane, the zoom note names the grid spacing drawn, and the flag is the same on either grid
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer’s motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
